Islands (leaves 2-3) are also fine, leading to identical turn 2 scenarios, but dual-land smoothness wins slightly. Mirror math: mana acceleration matters early.

Turn 1 main phase after land drop: Cast Three Steps Ahead (Spree, base {U}) requires paying for at least one mode. Cheapest is +{2} draw = {U}{2} total. This nets +1 card (draw 2, discard 1) for {2} generic mana, leaving me tapped out with nothing on board. In a mirror, this is too slow and doesn't advance my clock. Leaf 0 (pass): Hold mana and setup for turn 2 threat (Bat or Drowner). Mirrors are won on tempo and board development, not early card draw. Strongly prefer passing.

Pass priority. I've decided not to cast Three Steps Ahead (too slow, no value turn 1). I don't cast any threats on turn 1 in the mirror—I develop slowly and hold interaction up. Tapping Darkslick Shores for mana (options 2-3) without casting anything wastes the mana pool (it expires at end of phase). Proceed to combat (no attacks), postcombat main (pass again), then end step.

Begin Combat phase, same strategic situation. I have no creatures to attack with (will pass Declare Attackers empty). Casting Three Steps Ahead now instead of main phase has no tactical difference—it's still {U}{2} mana for +1 card, leaving me tapped with no board on turn 1. Mirror math: I should develop threats on turn 2 (Bat/Drowner), not burn mana on early card draw. Leaf 0 (pass): Preserve tempo and options. Leaf 1 (cast): Lose resources with no benefit.

Pass priority. No attackers (no creatures in play), so Begin Combat → Declare Attackers is empty. Passing moves to combat end steps, then postcombat main, then end step, then opponent's turn 1. Pass priority. No attackers declared (no creatures). This advances through combat damage → end combat → postcombat main → end step → opponent's turn 1. Save mana and cards for meaningful plays.
End Combat phase. Same situation repeating. I have no combat to resolve (no attackers, no damage). Casting Three Steps Ahead remains inefficient on turn 1. Pass to postcombat main, then end step.
Pass priority. Move to postcombat main phase.

Pass priority. End my turn 1 and move to end step, then opponent's turn 1.

End Turn phase (end step). Last priority window before opponent's turn 1 begins. Casting Three Steps Ahead now still offers no value—still just {U}{2} for +1 card. My turn 1 is complete; pass and move to opponent's turn 1 untapped and with full hand for turn 2 setup.
Pass priority. End my turn 1 and yield to opponent's turn 1.

Pass priority. Continue to Declare Attackers (opponent has no creatures) and opponent's combat phase.

Opponent's End Combat phase. No creatures attacked (empty combat). Passing is correct. Yielding until my turn 2 now.

My turn 3 upkeep. Finally my main turn to develop. Casting Three Steps Ahead on upkeep is still wasteful—no targets, no reason. Play a land immediately to develop tempo and threats.
